chunks: 1- Al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn ʿUthman, from ʿUmar ibn Yazid, who said:
I asked Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a man who dyes his head with henna, then decides to perform wudu (ablution). He said: He should wipe over the henna.

2- And with this isnad, from Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from Hammad ibn ʿUthman, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who shaves his head, then coats it with henna, then performs wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer), he said: There is no problem with his wiping his head while the henna is upon it.

3- As for what Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated, raising it to Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, concerning a man who dyes his head with henna and then decides to perform wudu (ablution), he said: It is not valid until the water reaches the skin of his head. The first issue with it is that it is mursal, with a broken isnad, and reports of this kind cannot be used to oppose musnad reports. Even if it were accepted, it could be understood to mean that if it is possible to make the water reach the skin, then it must be made to reach it; but if that is not possible, or hardship is involved in making it reach, then it is not obligatory upon him. And what confirms that is:
4- What Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli al-Washshaʾ, who said:
I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about medicine when it is on a man's hands: Is it sufficient for him to wipe over the coating of the medicine? He said: Yes, it is sufficient for him to wipe over it.

key_terms.الْأَخْبَارُ الْمُسْنَدَةُ: reports with connected chains of transmission
key_terms.الْحِنَّاءِ: henna applied to the head as a covering or dye
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification being discussed
key_terms.بَشَرَةَ رَأْسِهِ: the skin of his head, meaning direct contact of water with the scalp
key_terms.طِلَاءِ الدَّوَاءِ: the coating of medicine placed on the body
key_terms.مَقْطُوعُ الْإِسْنَادِ: having a broken chain of transmission
key_terms.مُرْسَلٌ: a report transmitted without a complete chain to the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.يَمْسَحُ: he wipes, referring to the prescribed wiping in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Can a person wipe over henna or medicinal coating during wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: These reports discuss the ruling of wiping in wudu (ablution) when henna or medicinal coating is present on the head or hands. The transmitted reports indicate the permissibility of wiping over such a covering, while also noting that if reaching the skin with water is possible without hardship, that may be required according to the reconciled understanding.
